title: Abaqus OFHC copper and 316-steel cyclic material paths
purpose: Verify AgentFEM's small-strain combined-hardening response against two numerical OFHC-copper observables published by SIMULIA, exercise the published 316-steel asymmetric stress path and one-versus-two-backstress ratcheting trend, then retain the native energy, result and restart lifecycle.
physics: three-dimensional small-strain J2 plasticity with tabulated isotropic hardening and one Armstrong--Frederick backstress under mixed stress--strain control

source.title: Simple proportional and nonproportional cyclic tests
source.case: OFHC copper symmetric uniaxial and nonproportional tension--torsion tests

related_sources.title: Uniaxial ratcheting under tension and compression
related_sources.case: 316 steel asymmetric stress cycle with one and two backstresses
related_sources.claim_boundary: The published maximum-strain response is graphical; current automation checks the exact path, control residual and published qualitative trend, not a digitized numerical Golden.

execution.evidence: The public benchmark reconstructs the published E, nu, calibrated C and gamma, tabulated cyclic hardening, exact reversal knots and stress-free transverse components.

observables: Equivalent plastic strain after the published symmetric cyclic path.
Maximum normal stress during the saturated nonproportional tension--torsion cycle.
Change in cycle maximum from the fourth to final simulated cycle.
Progressive maximum strain under the published 316-steel asymmetric stress path and the reduction obtained with two backstresses.
Axisymmetric global finite-element peak gauge strain versus the independent stress-controlled material-point path.
Discrete plastic-work, hardening-storage, recovery and numerical-dissipation ledger.
acceptance: Final PEEQ is within AgentFEM's 1% gate of the published Abaqus value 23.67%.
Saturated maximum normal stress is within AgentFEM's 1% gate of the published Abaqus value 143.1 MPa.
The fourth-to-final cycle maximum changes by less than AgentFEM's 1% saturation gate.
Both 316-steel calibrations accumulate positive ratchet strain and the published two-backstress calibration accumulates less than the one-backstress calibration.
A uniformly loaded axisymmetric tube matches the independent material-point peak strain within the declared AgentFEM cross-check tolerance and closes global equilibrium.
Every stress-controlled tensor component closes the local mixed-control residual.
limitations: The 1% acceptance limits are AgentFEM contracts, not SIMULIA-prescribed tolerances.
The 316-steel comparison is path/control/trend evidence because SIMULIA provides its maximum-strain response as a plot rather than a numerical table.
The uniform-tube finite-element case verifies global lowering but is not the published shouldered-specimen Golden.
This benchmark validates the calibrated material-point response; a structure-level ratcheting benchmark remains a separate promotion gate.
Temperature dependence, static recovery and cyclic softening remain outside this material implementation.
